html:
(4) Channel-capacity optimization: maximizing I(A;S′)I(A;S') over the action distribution p(a)p(a). Empowerment is not mere mutual information but the supremum of mutual information over all possible input (action) distributions–it is formally a channel capacity 1. This is a constrained optimization problem: find the p*(a)p^*(a) that maximizes I(At:t+k;St+k∣st)I(A_{t:t+k}; S_{t+k} \mid s_t) subject to the constraint that p(a)p(a) is a valid distribution. In classical information theory, this is solved by the Blahut–Arimoto algorithm, an iterative alternating-maximization procedure that converges to the capacity-achieving input distribution 2, 3. For continuous action spaces, variational lower bounds on mutual information provide a tractable alternative: variational information maximization replaces the intractable marginalization with a learned "planning" distribution qϕ(at:t+k∣st+k,st)q_\phi(a_{t:t+k} \mid s_{t+k}, s_t) that approximates the true posterior over actions given the achieved outcome, yielding a lower bound ℰ(st)≥𝔼p(a)p(s′|s,a)[log⁡qϕ(a∣s′,s)]+H(A)\mathcal{E}(s_t) \geq \mathbb{E}_{p(a)p(s'|s,a)}[\log q_\phi(a \mid s', s)] + H(A) that can be optimized end-to-end via gradient ascent 4. This variational formulation is significant because it factorizes the empowerment computation into two learnable components: a source model pθ(a∣s)p_\theta(a \mid s) that proposes actions (playing the role of the capacity-achieving input distribution), and a planning/inverse model qϕ(a∣s′,s)q_\phi(a \mid s', s) that "decodes" which action sequence was responsible for a given state transition (playing the role of the optimal receiver in the channel-coding analogy). Biologically, this decomposition maps naturally onto the distinction between a policy generator ("what actions are available from here?") and an inverse model ("what action would produce that outcome?")– both of which have well-attested neural substrates in premotor and cerebellar circuits 5, 6.

Neural architecture; how is it evolutionarily instantiated as an architectural prior?

The most "direct" biological substrate for channel-capacity optimization is the cortico-basal ganglia-thalamocortical (CBGTC) loop architecture, which evolution appears to have specialized as a generic distribution-shaping engine over actions. Rather than selecting a single motor command, basal ganglia circuits implement competition, normalization, and gating over action candidates proposed in cortex–exactly the kind of machinery needed to approximate an optimizer over p(a)p(a) under constraints (∑ap(a)=1\sum_ap(a)=1, nonnegativity). Striatum can represent many candidate policies in parallel from high-dimensional cortical state/context, while pallidal output and thalamic gating determine which channels are disinhibited, effectively reallocating probability mass over actions instead of executing a rigid argmax 7, 8, 9.

In the variational empowerment view, capacity optimization factorizes into a source/proposal policy pθ(at:t+k|st)p_\theta(a_{t:t+k}|s_t) and an inverse "decoder" qϕ(at:t+k|st+k,st)q_\phi(a_{t:t+k}|s_{t+k},s_t) that measures how uniquely an action sequence can be inferred from the resulting state (i.e., "decodability"). Neuroanatomically, pθp_\theta is naturally implemented by fronto-premotor policy manifolds (PMd/SMA/M1, plus parietal affordance maps) feeding into striatal channels that compete for gating. The key missing piece is qϕq_\phi: the brain needs circuitry that can rapidly answer "what action would have produced that outcome from this state?" and do so with graded uncertainty.

That inverse-model role is plausibly realized by a cerebellum + cortical inverse-model stack. The cerebellum is well-suited to act as an inverse/forward model workhorse because of its massive expansion of granule cells, supervised error-driven plasticity, and tight coupling to motor and premotor targets; classic sensorimotor-control accounts explicitly frame cerebellar modules as learning internal models that support both prediction and inversion (command inference) 6, 10, 5. But inverse modeling is not purely cerebellar: cortical circuits–especially posterior parietal cortex (PPC), premotor cortex, and prefrontal cortex–encode action goals, effectors, and action-effect mappings in a way that supports "goal->motor command(s)" transformations (e.g., reach-to-target transforms), providing a higher-level inverse model over abstract actions and outcomes, while cerebellum supplies fast, calibrated inversion at the fine-grained motor level 6, 5.

Inverse modeling matters because the variational lower bound contains 𝔼[logqϕ(a|s′,s)]\mathbb{E}[logq_\phi(a|s',s)]: it rewards policies whose outcomes make the responsible action easy to decode. Biologically, that "decodability reward" can be instantiated as inverse-model confidence/precision. When cerebellar + parietal/premotor inverse models return a sharp posterior over actions (high certainty about which command produced the transition), the system is implicitly detecting low conditional entropy H(S′|s,A)H(S'|s,A)’ when the inverse model is uncertain (many actions could have produced similar outcomes), conditional entropy is high. Thus, empowerment-relevant gradients can be supplied not by explicit MI computation but by how confidently the inverse stack can attribute outcomes to actions.

The basal ganglia then provide the optimization substrate that can use this signal. Cortico-striatal plasticity–shaped by dopamine–can reinforce action channels that yield transitions with high inverse-model confidence while maintaining diversity via neuromodulatory control of exploration "temperature." The STN-GP system (see "Cortico-Basal Ganglia-Thalamo-Cortical Loops") offers a stabilizing prior (global inhibition / threshold control) that prevents premature collapse of p(a)p(a) onto a single mode when multiple distinct futures are available, functionally resembling normalization/regularization in distributional optimization 11. In parallel, LC-NE (and tonic dopamine) can modulate gain and stochasticity, acting as the biological knob that trades off sharp exploitation vs high-entropy coverage 12, 13.

In sum, the evolutionary "architectural prior" is a three-part motif: (i) CBGTC loops that maintain and reshape a distribution over actions, (ii) a cerebellum + cortical inverse-model stack (cerebellar microcomplexes plus PPC/premotor goal-to-command transforms) that supplies a fast, graded decodability/precision signal approximating the logqϕlogq_\phi term, and (iii) neuromodulatory temperature control that keeps the optimizer from collapsing, enabling the system to approximate channel-capacity optimization without explicitly running Blahut-Arimoto in neural tissue 7, 6, 12.
